clue.text: Young female beauty initially with boy we rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the whole string of letters is read backwards
initially points to the opening letter of the word beauty

parts.note: a boy is a male
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman's beauty is mentioned alongside a boy who turned us down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young female' is the whole definition, a lamb of the female sex, not a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe lamb is a young sheep of the female sex, a direct description.

clue.text: Show two inspired by former success

parts.note: ex- is the prefix for former

indicators.note: to be inspired by something is to have it breathed in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hit is a success
bi- is the prefix meaning two

explanation.surface: A pair of people draw inspiration from a past triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: BI sits inside EXHIT, between the H and the IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exhibit is something put on display, as in a museum.

clue.text: Article I tailored for distribution

indicators.note: letters handed out for distribution are scattered and come back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has adapted an article ready to be sent out.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is the opinion piece in a newspaper, one kind of article.

clue.text: A time to divide work in suitable manner

indicators.note: the time letter splits the word for work, sitting in its middle

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade

explanation.surface: A moment is set aside to split up a task in a fitting way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means appropriately, in a way that suits the circumstances.

clue.text: Requiring surgery, a brief cut to split two ways

indicators.note: something needing an operation is in bad shape, so these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon's short incision divides tissue in two directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fork or divide into two branches.

clue.text: Car regularly entering station

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, so the frequent word sits inside the stopping place

parts.note: a stop is a station on a route
oft is an old word for often, regularly

explanation.surface: A car keeps pulling into the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but here it is the synonym OFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a convertible with a folding fabric roof is a kind of car.

clue.text: Fasten bits up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: bits are parts

explanation.surface: An instruction to tie pieces together securely.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap something is to fasten it with a band or belt.

clue.text: Sweet thing, one's nutty

definitions.meaning: a rich cake full of dried fruit, a sweet treat
slang for an eccentric or mad person

explanation.surface: A sweet treat that happens to contain nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a cake with dried fruit, and slang for a crazy person.

clue.text: Ultimately quiet, calm kid

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word quiet

parts.note: ease is calm, relaxation

explanation.surface: In the end, a peaceful, composed child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a noun, child, but is the verb meaning to joke with.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to kid someone is to tease them in fun.

clue.text: Bishop on time, it's suggested?

parts.note: being on time is being before late, so a churchman's title read in two parts hints at punctuality

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a bishop has turned up punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PRE-LATE, the word means 'before late', which is on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a senior churchman such as a bishop.

clue.text: Zero carried by this broken- down lift

indicators.note: the zero is carried inside the rearranged letters, as a load in a lift
a broken-down thing has fallen apart, so the letters of this are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Nothing gets carried by this lift, which has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' puts O inside HIST (the anagram of THIS).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hoist is to raise up, as with a crane.

clue.text: Lucky, finding strength to catch fish

indicators.note: the word for strength holds the fish, as a net would

parts.note: a forte is someone's strong point
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler is lucky to have the strength to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: blessed with good luck.

clue.text: Individual mistake backfiring, producing bomb perhaps?

indicators.note: something that backfires goes back the wrong way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a party is an individual person, as in a third party
a boob is a blunder

explanation.surface: One person's error went wrong and led to an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hidden bomb rigged to go off when disturbed is one kind of concealed device.

clue.text: Greek character grabbed by throat, he talked

indicators.note: the letters are held within these words, spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A Greek man is seized by the neck while speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and a character is a letter.

clue.text: Character demanding more surprising plot development

definitions.meaning: Oliver of the Dickens novel, the orphan who asks for more gruel
an unexpected turn in a story

explanation.surface: A demanding character drives an unexpected turn in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan Oliver famously asks for more, and the word also means a sudden turn in a plot.

clue.text: Redneck in the commercial, idiot

indicators.note: the bumpkin word sits inside the

parts.note: taken as written
a hick is a rural yokel
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A rural yokel stars in an advert, playing the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redneck' is US slang for a rural bumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dimwit, a stupid person.

clue.text: Across a street, right turn

parts.note: milk that turns goes sour; eggs that addle go bad

explanation.surface: Directions: cross a street, then turn right.
explanation.definitionFit: Straddling something means sitting with a leg on each side, so across it.

clue.text: Irritable about zealot not starting to produce evidence

indicators.note: the bad-tempered word goes around the shortened name

parts.note: testy means irritable

indicators.note: the apostle's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Simon the Zealot was one of the twelve apostles

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered fanatic is caught short of producing proof.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon the Zealot was one of the twelve apostles, so 'zealot' stands for his name; 'not starting' removes its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimony is a witness's statement, given as proof in court.

clue.text: Shakespeare, say, admits art creative

indicators.note: creative arrangement of the letters makes something new from them

explanation.surface: Shakespeare, for example, concedes that art is inventive.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Shakespeare is the best-known writer of plays.

clue.text: Witty quality beginning to evaporate, funny lass isn't entertaining?

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other
funny means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly
the beginning of evaporate is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl's wit fades away, and she is not amusing anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts E inside SALTINSS, the anagram of LASS ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty humour is earthy and sharp, so saltiness is a racy wit.

clue.text: Casanova rescued in a storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: The great lover is saved during a tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, is the byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Lift then not opening, almost everyone stuck inside

indicators.note: one piece is jammed within the other
the word for then loses its first letter

parts.note: next means then, after that

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A lift fails to open, and nearly everyone is trapped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to raise up, in rank or in praise.

clue.text: Table tops in some traditions layered in wood

indicators.note: the initials sit inside the word for wood

parts.note: a tree is the source of wood

indicators.note: the tops of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Tables made in layered wood, as some traditions have it.
explanation.walkthrough: S, T and L, from the first letters, go inside TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle table is a board laid across supports, and the word alone means such a table.

clue.text: Alien creation, valley with king

parts.note: a dale is a valley
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An alien world made up of a valley and its king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daleks are the alien robots devised for the TV series Doctor Who.

clue.text: In hotel one resides, as recluse

indicators.note: the letters lie within these three words

explanation.surface: A hermit lives quietly in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who keeps to themselves and avoids company.

clue.text: Cheese sandwiches good after drink, construction coming together

indicators.note: the cheese wraps round the filling like bread round a sandwich

parts.note: brie is a French cheese

indicators.note: the good letter is placed after the drink

parts.note: cola is a drink

explanation.surface: A cheese sandwich follows a drink while something is being built.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricolage is a construction made from whatever happens to be available.

clue.text: One surrounded by barking hounds

indicators.note: the single letter is enclosed by the word for mad

parts.note: barking and bats both mean crazy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by a pack of barking dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hounds' looks like the dogs, but is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to taunt and harass them, as to hound them.

clue.text: Primate's ending in the middle — the heart, say?

indicators.note: the primate's last letter is shifted into its centre

parts.note: an orang is an orangutan, a primate

explanation.surface: An ape's death sits at the centre of the matter, the heart of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the heart is one of the body's vital parts.

clue.text: Income set to change, in old money

indicators.note: the letters are to be changed into a different order

explanation.surface: Earnings are about to be altered into a former currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A centesimo was a small Italian coin, a hundredth of a lira.

clue.text: Criminality shining brightly, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that is the same when spoken

parts.note: gilt describes something gilded and gleaming

explanation.surface: A crime that glitters brightly, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt is the fact of having committed a crime.

clue.text: Respecting cardinal, very large screen

parts.note: re means about, respecting
cardinal is a deep red colour
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A huge screen pays tribute to a cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Ending in custody, agent touring around unknown river

indicators.note: the ending of custody is its last letter
the shuffled letters go round the unknown
touring means moving about, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A spy on tour is finally arrested near a mysterious river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts Z inside ANGTE, the anagram of AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river.
